title: Albanian Alps to the Riviera
subRegion: Shkodër, Theth, Vlorë & the Albanian Riviera

bestPeriod.avoid: November–April (SH21 to Theth is snowbound and guesthouses shut); late July–August brings 38°C heat and bumper-to-bumper Riviera traffic

accommodation.note: Guesthouse half-board in Theth; mid-range sea-view rooms in Sarandë

food.note: Byrek and grilled fish are cheap; Ksamil beach clubs are not

transport.note: Rental incl. CDW, fuel, Llogara tunnel toll, Koman ferry, parking

activities.note: Butrint, Rozafa, Theth NP, Blue Eye, Porto Palermo

profile.difficultyNote: 2 — driving-led, with optional 2–4 h valley walks in Theth and a flat 2 km loop at Butrint

gatewayAirport: TIA — Tirana International "Nënë Tereza"; 95 km / 1 h 40 to Shkodër on SH1
summary: This is the drive that shows you two Albanias in one week: the limestone Accursed Mountains where the tarmac ran out until recently, and the Ionian coast where it now runs beautifully. You begin on the flat SH1 to Shkodër, spend a day on the fjord-like Lake Koman ferry, then climb the reengineered SH21 through the Thore tunnel into Theth, a stone village under 2,500 m walls. A long transfer day drops you to the Adriatic at Vlorë, after which the Riviera unrolls — the Llogara Pass at 1,027 m, the Ottoman gunpowder bay at Porto Palermo, Butrint's Roman theatre in the marshes. It suits confident drivers who accept single-track sections, unlit tunnels and the occasional cow, and who want landscape density that Western Europe cannot match at this price.

itinerary.title: Tirana tarmac to the Rozafa ramparts
itinerary.morning: Collect the car airside at TIA and get out of the terminal loop before the Tirana rush thickens. The SH1 north is dual carriageway most of the way to Lezhë, then narrows; expect unsignalled U-turn lanes and mopeds using the hard shoulder as a lane.
itinerary.afternoon: Reach Shkodër by early afternoon and drive straight up to Rozafa Castle before the light hardens — the ramparts sit above the confluence of the Drin, Buna and Kir, and the free car park inside the lower gate saves a hot walk. Then park the car for the night and walk Rruga Kolë Idromeno, the pedestrianised Ottoman-Italianate spine.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Tradita Geg & Tosk, in a restored 18th-century house with a stone courtyard — order the smoked trout from the Drin and the fërgesë.
itinerary.dayStats: 95 km / 1 h 40 driving; Rozafa entry 400 ALL (~€4); zero tolls; sea level throughout.
itinerary.sleep: Rooms Tradita, Shkodër — walled parking inside the property.

itinerary.title: The Koman fjord, on foot
itinerary.morning: Leave Shkodër by 07:15. The SH25 runs via Vau i Dejës and Koman; the final 20 km is a shelf road with rockfall debris and that unlit tunnel. Leave the car in the paid lot at the dam (300–500 ALL) and board the 09:00 Berisha ferry as a foot passenger — three hours of near-vertical schist walls with cable ferries dropping villagers on shingle beaches.
itinerary.afternoon: The boat reaches Fierza around 11:45. Eat at the quayside café, then take the 13:00 return, which gives you the same gorge with the light on the opposite wall. Back at Koman by ~15:45.
itinerary.evening: Drive back to Shkodër (1 h 30) and take an aperitivo on Sheshi Nënë Tereza. Dinner at Restaurant Vila Bekaj for grilled carp.
itinerary.dayStats: 130 km round trip / 3 h driving; 6 h afloat; ferry €9 pp online; parking ~€4; no fuel between Vau i Dejës and Koman.
itinerary.sleep: Rooms Tradita, Shkodër (second night — leave heavy luggage in the room).

itinerary.title: SH21 and the Thore tunnel into Theth
itinerary.morning: Head north on SH1 then fork onto SH21 at Koplik. The climb through Dedaj and Boga is the good part: smooth new asphalt, long sightlines, karst towers. Stop at the Boga plateau layby for coffee.
itinerary.afternoon: Through the Thore tunnel and into the Theth basin on a descent of tight, walled bends. Once in the village, park at your guesthouse and walk to the Church of Theth and the 17th-century Kulla e Ngujimit (lock-in tower) — a working monument to the Kanun blood-feud code.
itinerary.evening: Half-board at your guesthouse is standard and genuinely good: cornbread, fresh cheese, honey, mountain tea. There is one small bar by the church; the valley goes dark early.
itinerary.dayStats: 68 km / 2 h 15; highest point of SH21 ~1,630 m at the tunnel approach; last fuel at Koplik; village lanes are gravel.
itinerary.sleep: Bujtina Polia, Theth — stone guesthouse with off-road parking on grass.

itinerary.title: Blue Eye of Theth, then a long run to the sea
itinerary.morning: Walk or 4x4-shuttle to the Blue Eye of Theth (Syri i Kaltër i Thethit) — 6 km each way from Ndërlysaj on a rough track; the last 25 minutes is a scramble. Do not attempt the track in a low 2WD; the village shuttles charge ~1,500 ALL (~€15) return.
itinerary.afternoon: This is the transfer. Retrace SH21 to Koplik, SH1 south past Lezhë, then the A1/SH2 corridor via Durrës and the SH4 to Vlorë. The Durrës ring is the one genuinely stressful stretch: aggressive undertaking, poor lane discipline.
itinerary.evening: Arrive Vlorë for sunset on the Lungomare. Dinner at Restaurant Nertili on the waterfront — whole sea bass by weight, priced per kilo.
itinerary.dayStats: 315 km / 6 h 15 including the Blue Eye detour; no tolls; fill up at Lezhë; Vlorë hotel parking often €5/night.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Regina City, Vlorë — secure underground garage, five minutes from the promenade.

itinerary.title: Llogara Pass and the Riviera
itinerary.morning: Drive south via Orikum, where the road lifts away from the Karaburun lagoon. Take the SH8 up to the Llogara Pass rather than the tunnel. The Caesar's Pass viewpoint by Hotel Alpin, and the paragliding launch above it, give the best of the Karaburun panorama — go before 10:00 while the haze is thin and the sun is still behind you.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend to Dhërmi and Vuno, then Himarë. Turn off for Porto Palermo, where Ali Pasha's triangular fortress sits on a causeway in a near-perfect bay. Entry is a few hundred lek; the naval base next door means no drones.
itinerary.evening: Continue to Sarandë (SH8 hugging the cliffs above Borsh and Lukovë). Dinner at Taverna Laberia, above the port, for lamb tavë kosi and a Kallmet red.
itinerary.dayStats: 120 km / 3 h 30 with stops; Llogara summit 1,027 m; ~20 hairpins on the north side; tunnel alternative 250 ALL; steep 8–10% gradients on the Palasë descent — use engine braking.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Butrinti & Spa, Sarandë — one of the few central hotels with its own gated car park.

itinerary.title: Butrint, the Blue Eye and Ksamil
itinerary.morning: Be at Butrint National Park for opening. The drive down the Ksamil road takes 25 minutes; park at the site lot. The Greek theatre, the baptistery mosaics (usually under protective sand) and the Venetian tower reward two hours.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross on the Vivari Channel cable ferry (a genuine chain ferry, ~500 ALL for a car) to the Ali Pasha castle, then drive inland to the Blue Eye of Muzinë on the SH99 — a 50 m-deep karst spring. The final 2 km is a rough unsealed track; there is a paid lot at the entrance.
itinerary.evening: Back to Sarandë; sundowners at Mare Nostrum on the promenade, then dinner at Haxhi seafood.
itinerary.dayStats: 90 km / 2 h driving; Butrint 1,200 ALL (~€12); Blue Eye 200 ALL plus 200 ALL parking; ferry 500 ALL.

itinerary.title: Gjirokastër stone city and the run to Tirana
itinerary.morning: Climb inland on the SH99 through the Muzinë pass to Gjirokastër. Park below the bazaar — the upper old town lanes are cobbled at 15% gradient and will punish a rental clutch. The castle, the Skenduli House and the Zekate House are the three worth your time.
itinerary.afternoon: North on SH4 through the Drino valley, joining the A2 Levan–Vlorë motorway and then the SH4 to Tirana. Traffic thickens hard from Fier onward.
itinerary.evening: Drop the car at TIA with a full tank (there is a station 3 km before the terminal on the airport spur; airport refuelling charges are punitive).
itinerary.dayStats: 285 km / 4 h 45; Gjirokastër castle 400 ALL; Muzinë pass ~570 m; no tolls on this routing.
itinerary.sleep: Departure, or Hotel Mondial, Tirana if you fly out on Day 8.

accommodationStrategy.name: Rooms Tradita
accommodationStrategy.description: Two nights here bookends the northern half of the trip without repacking, and the enclosed courtyard parking matters in a city where street parking is contested and opportunistic. Breakfast starts at 07:00, early enough for the Koman ferry run. Roughly €55–€75 a double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Bujtina Polia
accommodationStrategy.description: Half-board is the point: there is effectively no restaurant economy in Theth, and dinner at 19:30 with the family is the experience. Flat grass parking beside the house avoids the deeply rutted lanes further up the valley. About €50–€70 per person with dinner and breakfast.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Butrinti & Spa
accommodationStrategy.description: Chosen almost entirely for the gated car park, which removes the single biggest headache of a Riviera summer. It is a five-minute walk from the promenade, has a sea-facing pool for the dead hours of the afternoon, and sits on the correct side of town for the Butrint road. €90–€150 a double in shoulder season.

logistics.connectivity: Albania is **not** in the EU roaming zone, though Vodafone, One and some EU operators now include it in "Western Balkans" bundles — check before you land or buy a Vodafone AL tourist SIM (~€10 for 20 GB). There is no signal for most of the Koman gorge and patchy coverage in Theth. Download offline maps for the whole north.
logistics.emergency: 112 works nationally; 127 is the ambulance line and 129 the police. Mountain rescue in the Accursed Mountains is informal — guesthouses and the Theth NP ranger post coordinate. Confirm your travel insurance explicitly covers Albania and non-EU medical repatriation; many EU-only policies do not.
logistics.weather: Afternoon thunderstorms build over the Accursed Mountains from roughly 14:00 in June and September, and they close the Theth road with mud and rockfall for hours at a time. On the Riviera, a strong northwesterly can make the Llogara descent gusty enough to move a high-sided car.
logistics.bookingWindows: Theth guesthouses fill 4–6 weeks ahead for June and September weekends. Book the Koman ferry online 3–5 days ahead if taking a car (bookferryberisha.com); as a foot passenger you can usually walk on. Butrint needs no advance ticket.
logistics.money: Currency is the lek (ALL), ~100 ALL ≈ €1. Cards work in Tirana, Shkodër and Sarandë hotels; assume cash-only in Theth, at the ferry, at rural fuel stations and for all parking. Withdraw from Credins or Raiffeisen ATMs and decline dynamic currency conversion. Tipping is rounding up, or 5–10% for a real meal.
logistics.transportRules: No vignette. Headlights are mandatory day and night. The alcohol limit is 0.01% — effectively zero. Speed cameras are concentrated on the SH1 and the Fier bypass, and rental companies pass fines on with a €25–€40 admin charge. Cross-border into Montenegro or Greece requires a Green Card and the agency's written permission letter; get both in writing at pickup.
logistics.permits: Theth is a national park — camping requires permission and open fires are banned. Drones are prohibited over Porto Palermo, Butrint and all military installations, and Albania requires registration for drones above 250 g. Butrint is a UNESCO site with no drone use at all.
logistics.health: Tap water is chlorinated and generally safe in cities but tastes poor; most travellers buy bottled. Spring water in Theth is drinkable. Ticks are present in the northern beech forests May–July. There is no altitude concern on this route. Sea urchins are common on the rocky Riviera entries — bring reef shoes.

proTips: Do the Koman ferry as a **foot passenger round trip** rather than shipping the car. You see the same gorge twice in different light, save €35–€40, and avoid the fact that the Fierza side commits you to a 230 km return via Kukës.

Drive the Llogara Pass **northbound to southbound in the morning**. The Karaburun reveal happens on the descent, and before 10:00 the sun is behind you rather than burning straight into the windscreen.
In Theth, arrange the Blue Eye 4x4 shuttle the night before through your guesthouse. Walk-up prices at Ndërlysaj are roughly 40% higher and the vehicles fill by 09:00.
Fuel discipline: treat Koplik, Lezhë, Orikum and Delvinë as your mandatory fill points. Rural pumps are often attended-only, cash-only, and closed by 20:00.

Sarandë's promenade parking is aggressively ticketed by informal attendants. Pay the €2–€3, take the paper slip, and never leave anything visible — smash-and-grab is the one real property crime on this coast.
Ksamil is a car trap in July and August; the beach clubs' access lanes gridlock by 11:00. Go at 08:00 or skip it for Pulëbardha beach, 3 km north, which has a proper lot.

Buy your Vodafone AL SIM at the airport arrivals kiosk, not in town — the tourist bundle is only sold at certain outlets and it is the difference between having and not having navigation in the north.
Photograph Porto Palermo in the late afternoon, when the sun rakes across the fortress walls from the west and the bay turns navy. Mornings there are flat and backlit.

raw.Total distance: ~1,050 km over 7 days; 5 driving days, 2 largely static. Longest leg is Day 4, Theth–Vlorë, 315 km in a genuine 6 h 15 including stops.
raw.SH21 (Shkodër–Theth), 68 km: fully asphalted since the Thore tunnel opened, but it is a 2-lane-becomes-1.5-lane mountain road with unguarded drops above Boga and roughly 30 tight bends on the descent into Theth. Allow 2 h 15, not the 1 h 20 your phone claims. A normal hatchback manages it in dry weather; a compact SUV with real ground clearance is worth the €10–15/day for the unpaved village spurs inside Theth itself.
raw.Llogara Pass, SH8, 1,027 m: the classic climb from Dukat with ~20 broad hairpins and a sudden reveal of the Karaburun peninsula. The 5.9 km Llogara Tunnel now bypasses it (250 ALL / ~€2.50 for a car, electronic gates, 24/7). Take the tunnel only if weather has closed the pass — the pass is the reason you came, and it costs nothing.
raw.Lake Koman ferry: Berisha operates daily 15 April–5 November; Koman→Fierza departs 09:00, Fierza→Koman 13:00. Foot passengers €9 online / €10 cash; cars are priced by footprint at €7/m² online (a typical compact ≈ €33–€40). The access road SH25 from Vau i Dejës to the Koman dam ends in a 300 m unlit rock tunnel with no lighting and no markings — headlights on, hold the crown of the road.
raw.Cross-border rental rules: Albania is outside the EU and outside the Green Card free-circulation zone for many policies. Most Tirana agencies (Enterprise, Sixt, and the reliable local Ada Rent) permit Montenegro, Kosovo, North Macedonia and Greece for a cross-border fee of €30–€60 plus a Green Card issued at the desk; Serbia and Bosnia are frequently excluded. One-way drops back to TIA are usually free; drops in Sarandë carry €60–€120.
raw.Fuel gaps: there is no reliable fuel between Shkodër and Theth (68 km), none between Koman dam and Vau i Dejës, and the stretch from Llogara down to Himarë has only small independent stations that sometimes run dry in August. Kastrati and Bolv-Oil stations are the dependable brands. Fill at every opportunity above half a tank in the north.
raw.Tolls & vignettes: Albania has no vignette. Tolls exist only on the Llogara Tunnel and the Rrëshen–Kalimash (Kalimash tunnel) motorway toward Kosovo, which this route avoids. Currency is the lek (ALL); ~100 ALL ≈ €1.

sources.verified: Llogara Tunnel status, 2026 toll (250 ALL / ~€2.50) and the fact that the free 1,027 m pass road remains open; Lake Koman Berisha ferry 2026 season (15 April–5 November), 09:00 Koman and 13:00 Fierza departures, and 2026 passenger/vehicle pricing; SH21 Theth road asphalt status and its mid-November to late-March/April seasonal closure; Albania's absence of a national vignette.
sources.confidenceNotes: Koman ferry timings shift with water level and operator, and a second operator sometimes runs a competing schedule — re-verify departure times within a week of travel. Albanian entry fees (Butrint, Rozafa, Blue Eye) are raised without notice and should be re-checked annually. Cross-border rental permissions and Green Card fees vary by agency and change frequently; the €30–€60 band is indicative, not quoted. The Llogara Pass has no fixed closure dates but can shut for 1–7 days after December–February snowfall. Fuel-station brands and locations in the far north change; treat the named fill points as minimums, not guarantees.
